# Model heterogeneity, step 6: does the crossover cut follow the prose number across the whole range?

*Branch `model-heterogeneity`. No GA, no fitness. Driver `experiments/run_cut_number_sweep.py`, tables generated by `experiments/summarize_cut_number_sweep.py` from `results/raw/` (`sequence_operator_compliance_<model>_len63_cutnum_segex_prose<N>.json`, `llm_operator_calls_cutnum_prose<N>_<model>.jsonl`, console and driver logs). The tables below are the generated file `results/raw/model_cutnum_tables.md`, unedited.*

## Question and design

Steps 2 and 3 tried two prose numbers only, 40 (as shipped) and 25. Here the prose number N in "a boundary at N falls N% of the way along Parent 1 and N% of the way along Parent 2" is varied over 10, 25, 37, 60, 90 (37 deliberately not round; 10 and 90 near the extremes), with the worked example removed from the prompt and the retry hint in every setting, so N is the only thing that changes.

`qwen2.5:7b` (0% fallback in steps 1-3) and `gemma4:12b` (went to the midpoint, 50, when the prose said 25). 100 `crossover/segment` calls per model per N, genome length 63, bounds [30, 80], temperature 0.7, seed 0, `num_ctx` 4096: the step 1-3 settings. Each setting restarts the probe's RNG at seed 0, so with no fallbacks every setting of a model sees the same 100 parent pairs. The probe and `hpga/` are not edited; the driver wraps the probe's example-removal helper and prose text for its own process. The N=25 prompt and retry hint were checked offline to be byte-identical to the probe's earlier `absent_prose25` (`--check-equivalence`), and the `qwen2.5:7b` N=25 run reproduces step 2's cut distribution exactly (25x100, 75x11, 50x1).

Definitions: a cut is an interior boundary in the valid reply of an LLM-successful call (a 3-segment reply has two). "Calls containing N" and "calls whose only cut is N" are out of 100 calls; the second is the strictest reading of "the cut equals the prose number". The first-attempt lists read the first reply of every call, valid or not, from the call log.

## Results (generated)

100 crossover/segment calls per cell, genome length 63, bounds [30, 80], temperature 0.7, seed 0, worked example removed in every setting, prose sentence 'a boundary at N falls N% of the way ...' with N as shown. 99 possible cuts.

## Reading the results

**Fallback and format.** 0/100 in all ten cells. Requests per call 1.00-1.04. Every reply used the requested format; what changes across N is only which cut is named.

**`qwen2.5:7b`: follows N over 25-60, does not at 10 and largely not at 90.**

| prose N | cut = N | modal cut |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | 1 of 107 cuts (1 call of 100) | 30 (67%) |
| 25 | 100 of 112 (100 calls) | 25 (89% of cuts; the rest is a second cut at 75 in 11 three-segment replies) |
| 37 (not round) | 100 of 100 | 37 (100%, one distinct value) |
| 60 | 97 of 100 | 60 (97%; 3 at 40) |
| 90 | 31 of 120 (31 calls) | 30 (59%) |

The non-round 37 is followed in 100 of 100 calls, so the effect is not specific to round numbers. At the two extremes it breaks: at N=10 the cut is 10 in one call, and 30 (72 of 100 first replies) instead; at N=90 the cut is 90 in 31 calls and 30 in 71. The 30 is not a number written in the prose in those settings; it is, however, the lower length bound printed in the same prompt ("between 30 and 80 letters long"). That is a candidate explanation only and was not tested; an informal comparison of group means found the mean shorter-parent length equal at N=10 (44.8 in both groups) and a few letters apart at N=90 (49.6 where the cut was 90, 43.4 where it was 30); no test was run, so this neither supports nor rules out a dependence on the parents.

**`gemma4:12b`: follows 60 (90 of 100) and, partly, 37 (27 of 100); at 10, 25 and 90 it never uses N.**

| prose N | cut = N | modal cut |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | 0 of 100 | 50 (96%; 4 at 40) |
| 25 | 0 of 100 | 50 (100%) |
| 37 | 27 of 100 | 50 (73%) |
| 60 | 90 of 100 | 60 (90%; 10 at 50) |
| 90 | 0 of 100 | 50 (100%) |

So `gemma4:12b` does sometimes follow the number: at 60 in 90 calls, at 37 in 27. It never goes to the number at 10, 25 or 90. The values it follows (37 and 60) are within 13 of the midpoint; the ones it does not (25, 10, 90) are 25 or more away. That pattern is consistent with a window around the midpoint but it rests on five values with nothing tested between 25 and 37 or between 60 and 90, so the window's edge is not located. Cuts are always single (100 of 100 declarations have two segments in every cell).

**A 40 without a 40 in the prompt.** With the example gone and the prose at 10, 60 or 90, a cut of 40 appears: `qwen2.5:7b` 9 of 107 cuts at N=10, 3 at N=60, 4 at N=90; `gemma4:12b` 4 of 100 at N=10. Only one of these 20 calls has a parent of length exactly 40 (the `qwen2.5:7b` N=90 call with parents 41 and 40); the replies are typically exactly `SEGMENTS: 0-40:1, 40-100:2`, the text of the removed worked example. All 40s occur in cells where the model is not following N (none at N=25 or 37 in either model). This qualifies the step-2 statement that no model keeps 40 when no 40 is in the prompt: at N=25 that still holds (0 of 112 and 0 of 100), but where the prose number is ignored a small residual of 40 (3% to 8% of cuts) returns. Its source (the model's own habit, or a trace of the removed example) is not determined here.

**Prompt check.** Every logged attempt of every cell contains the prose sentence with the stated N and no `e.g.`; no attempt contains N anywhere else in the prompt, except that a parent of length 37 or 60 is printed as data in 4 headers of the N=37 and N=60 cells (in both models, same parent pairs). Those 4 headers are visible in the table; they did not stop N=37 or N=60 from being followed.

## Limits

- One seed and 100 calls per cell; the same 100 parent pairs in every cell of a model, so differences between cells are prompt effects, not sampling of the parents. A single-seed cell can move by a few percent on a rerun (step 3 note).
- Two models. `llama3.2:3b` and `mistral:7b` were not swept; `mistral:7b` was already fragile to prompt changes (47/100 fallback at N=25 in step 2).
- Five values of N, no worked example anywhere. Whether the breakdown of `qwen2.5:7b` at 90 (and 10) sets in at, say, 75 or 85 is not located; nor is `gemma4:12b`'s window. N=10 and N=90 are both extreme and far from the midpoint, so "extreme" and "far from 50" cannot be told apart with these values.
- Why `qwen2.5:7b` falls to 30 at the extremes is untested (the length-bound candidate above).
- The example was removed in every cell, so the sweep does not say what happens to the residual pull of an example that contradicts the prose number, only that the prose number carries the cut where it carries it.
